qianlong-bluete-der-qing#text: Qianlong reigned from 1735 to 1796 and extended the empire through campaigns into Central Asia, Tibet, and the southwest. The population grew to around 300 million, and the emperor had an enormous collection of Chinese literature compiled. Toward European wishes for trade, China remained closed; in 1793 Qianlong turned away a British embassy with the remark that his empire had no need of foreign goods.
oesterreichischer-erbfolgekrieg#title: Maria Theresa and the War of the Austrian Succession
oesterreichischer-erbfolgekrieg#summary: After the death of Emperor Charles VI, Prussia, Bavaria, and France attack the inheritance of the 23-year-old Maria Theresa, who holds on to her lands except for Silesia.
oesterreichischer-erbfolgekrieg#text: Charles VI had secured his daughter's succession with the Pragmatic Sanction, but he had hardly died in October 1740 when Frederick II of Prussia invaded the wealthy province of Silesia, and Bavaria and France put forward claims of their own. Maria Theresa won the support of the Hungarian estates, raised new armies, and in 1745 secured the election of her husband Francis Stephen as emperor. The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle in 1748 confirmed her possessions but left Silesia with Prussia. From the defeat she drew the conclusion that the administration, army, taxes, and school system of her lands had to be fundamentally reformed.
montesquieu-geist-der-gesetze#title: Montesquieu publishes The Spirit of the Laws
montesquieu-geist-der-gesetze#summary: Charles de Montesquieu calls for the separation of legislative, executive, and judicial power in order to secure liberty against the abuse of power.
montesquieu-geist-der-gesetze#text: The baron from Bordeaux had spent twenty years comparing the constitutions, climates, customs, and laws of different peoples, and had traveled in England. In his work, printed in Geneva, he described the English constitution as a model, because there the king, parliament, and independent courts limited one another; where all power lies in one hand, he wrote, there is no liberty. He distinguished between republic, monarchy, and despotism and warned against arbitrary rule. Although the church placed the book on the Index in 1751, it was read throughout Europe and influenced the Constitution of the United States of 1787 as well as the French revolutionaries.
erste-baende-der-encyclopedie#title: The first volumes of the Encyclopédie appear
erste-baende-der-encyclopedie#summary: Denis Diderot and Jean le Rond d'Alembert publish the first volume of the great encyclopedia of the Enlightenment in Paris.
erste-baende-der-encyclopedie#text: The Encyclopédie was to gather the entire knowledge of the age, from philosophy to the crafts, and make it accessible to reason. More than 140 authors, among them Voltaire, Rousseau, and Montesquieu, wrote articles that often criticized the church and absolutism in veiled form. Despite bans and censorship, the work grew by 1772 to 28 volumes with more than 70,000 articles and was read throughout Europe.
erdbeben-von-lissabon#summary: On All Saints' Day, an earthquake, a tidal wave, and fires destroy the Portuguese capital and set off a debate across Europe about God and nature.
erdbeben-von-lissabon#text: On the morning of 1 November 1755, when the churches were full, a tremendous earthquake shook Lisbon; tidal waves flooded the harbor, and fires raged for days. Estimates range from 30,000 to 60,000 dead, and one of the richest cities in Europe lay in ruins. The minister Pombal organized rescue and reconstruction with earthquake-resistant buildings and had the causes investigated scientifically. In a poem and in Candide, Voltaire mocked the idea that everything in the world is ordered for the best, Rousseau contradicted him, and Kant wrote three treatises on the natural causes of earthquakes.
siebenjaehriger-krieg#summary: Prussia and Great Britain fight against Austria, France, and Russia in a war waged in Europe, America, and India.
siebenjaehriger-krieg#text: Frederick II of Prussia opened the war with the invasion of Saxony and held his own against superior forces, but he came close to defeat several times; the death of the Russian tsarina Elizabeth in 1762 saved him. In North America and India, Great Britain defeated France and took over Canada as well as supremacy in Bengal. Prussia kept Silesia and rose to become a European great power.
vertreibung-der-jesuiten-1767#title: Expulsion of the Jesuits from Spanish America
vertreibung-der-jesuiten-1767#summary: King Charles III has the Jesuits expelled from all Spanish lands; the Guaraní reductions decline.
vertreibung-der-jesuiten-1767#text: To the enlightened ministers of the Bourbons the Jesuit order seemed too powerful, too rich and too bound to the pope; Portugal had already banished it from its empire in 1759. In the summer of 1767 more than two thousand Jesuits in Spanish America were arrested and shipped to Europe. Their schools, haciendas and missions passed to the Crown or to other orders. In Mexico there were protests, which were violently suppressed. Many expelled Creole Jesuits wrote works on the history of their American homeland in exile in Italy.
cooks-pazifikreisen#summary: On three voyages James Cook surveys New Zealand, the east coast of Australia, and countless islands of the Pacific, and ends the search for the southern continent.
cooks-pazifikreisen#text: On the commission of the Royal Society, Cook observed the transit of Venus on Tahiti in 1769, then sailed around New Zealand and in 1770 landed in Botany Bay on the east coast of Australia, which he claimed for Great Britain. On the second voyage he was the first to cross the Antarctic Circle and proved that there was no habitable southern continent; on the third he reached Hawaii, where he was killed in a dispute with local people in 1779. With a chronometer, sauerkraut against scurvy, and naturalists such as Joseph Banks and Georg Forster on board, his voyages turned exploration into a science. For the inhabitants of Australia and the Pacific islands, European colonization began with them.
watts-dampfmaschine#title: James Watt improves the steam engine
watts-dampfmaschine#summary: The Scottish instrument maker James Watt receives a patent for a steam engine with a separate condenser.
watts-dampfmaschine#text: Thomas Newcomen's steam engine had been used since 1712 to pump water out of mines, but it consumed enormous quantities of coal. Watt recognized that the steam should be condensed in a separate vessel so that the cylinder stays hot; this reduced fuel consumption by about three quarters. Together with the entrepreneur Matthew Boulton he built engines from 1775 onward that soon drove factories, mills, and mines.
frieden-von-kuecuek-kaynarca#summary: After a heavy defeat by Russia, the Ottoman Empire loses its suzerainty over the Crimea and opens the Black Sea to Russian ships.
frieden-von-kuecuek-kaynarca#text: In the Russo-Ottoman War from 1768 the armies of Catherine the Great had defeated the Ottomans on the Danube and in 1770 destroyed their fleet at Çeşme. On 21 July 1774 peace was concluded in the Bulgarian village of Küçük Kaynarca. The Crimean Khanate became independent and was annexed by Russia in 1783; Russian merchant ships were allowed to sail the Black Sea and the Straits. Russia later derived a right of protection over the Orthodox Christians from the treaty. At the same time the sultan, as caliph, was named for the first time in a treaty as religious head of the Muslims.
amerikanische-unabhaengigkeitserklaerung: On 4 July 1776, thirteen British colonies declare themselves the independent United States of America.

The dispute with London over taxes and representation had turned into open fighting in 1775. The text, written by Thomas Jefferson, justified the separation by the inalienable rights of all people to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. After the victory at Yorktown in 1781, Great Britain recognized independence in 1783; in 1787 the states gave themselves a federal constitution.
aufstand-tupac-amaru-ii#title: The uprising of Túpac Amaru II
aufstand-tupac-amaru-ii#summary: An Indigenous cacique from the region of Cusco leads the largest uprising against Spanish colonial rule in the 18th century.
aufstand-tupac-amaru-ii#text: José Gabriel Condorcanqui, who named himself after the last Inca ruler Túpac Amaru, had a hated colonial official arrested and executed in November 1780. He demanded the abolition of the mita and of the forced sales through which officials exploited the population. Tens of thousands of Indigenous people and mestizos joined him; his wife Micaela Bastidas organised supplies and troops. In April 1781 both were captured, and in May they were cruelly executed in Cusco. The uprising continued in the highlands until 1782 and cost tens of thousands of lives.
mechanischer-webstuhl-fabriksystem#title: The power loom and the factory system
mechanischer-webstuhl-fabriksystem#summa: Spinning machines and the power loom move textile production out of the home and into the factory.
mechanischer-webstuhl-fabriksystem#text: With James Hargreaves's spinning jenny of the 1760s, one worker could operate several spindles at once, Richard Arkwright's water frame used water power from 1769, and in 1785 Edmund Cartwright patented the power loom. Because the machines were tied to a central source of power, large factories arose such as Arkwright's mill at Cromford, in which hundreds of people worked to fixed hours and under supervision. The handloom weavers could not compete with the cheap factory cloth and fell into poverty. The factory system spread from the cotton industry to all branches of industry and has shaped the world of work to this day.
verfassung-der-usa#title: The Constitution of the United States
verfassung-der-usa#summary: In Philadelphia the delegates of the states adopt the first modern written constitution, with a separation of powers and an elected president.
verfassung-der-usa#text: After the War of Independence the thirteen states formed only a loose confederation without powers of taxation or trade, which led to debt, unrest, and quarrels. From May to September 1787, 55 delegates under the chairmanship of George Washington deliberated on a new order in Philadelphia behind closed doors; James Madison is regarded as its most important architect. The constitution divided power between a Congress of two chambers, a president, and a Supreme Court, and between the federal government and the individual states; a compromise counted enslaved people as three fifths for the allocation of seats and thereby entrenched slavery. After fierce debates it came into force in 1789, and in 1791 ten amendments, the Bill of Rights, added basic rights such as freedom of speech, of the press, and of religion. The constitution remains in force, with amendments, to this day.
erklaerung-der-menschen-und-buergerrecht: The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
On 26 August 1789 the National Assembly proclaims liberty, equality, and the sovereignty of the people as basic rights.

In 17 articles the assembly declared that all human beings are born free and equal in rights, that all state power proceeds from the people, and that freedom of opinion and of religion, property, and protection against arbitrary treatment are to be guaranteed. Women, slaves, and those without property remained excluded at first; in 1791 Olympe de Gouges responded with a Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen. The declaration became a model for constitutions all over the world.
frauenmarsch-nach-versailles#summary: Thousands of Parisian women march to Versailles because of the shortage of bread and force the royal family to move to Paris.
frauenmarsch-nach-versailles#text: In the autumn of 1789 the price of bread rose in Paris, while the king had still not confirmed the resolutions of the National Assembly, and rumors of a banquet held by the guard at Versailles increased the anger. On 5 October some 7,000 women of the market halls, armed with pikes and kitchen knives, marched the twenty kilometers to Versailles in the rain; the National Guard under Lafayette followed them. After the palace was stormed during the night, in which members of the bodyguard were killed, Louis XVI had to sign the Declaration of the Rights of Man and move with his family to the Tuileries in Paris, where the National Assembly followed as well. From then on the king stood before the eyes of the people, and women had shown themselves to be a political force of the revolution.
sturm-auf-die-bastille#summary: On 14 July 1789 the people of Paris storm the royal prison, marking the beginning of the French Revolution.
sturm-auf-die-bastille#text: After the Third Estate had declared itself the National Assembly and the king had gathered troops around Paris, the population armed itself. The Bastille held only a few prisoners but was regarded as a symbol of royal arbitrariness. Its fall forced Louis XVI to give way; throughout the country peasants rose against their landlords, and in August the National Assembly abolished feudal rights.
beginn-der-haitianischen-revolution#titl: The beginning of the Haitian Revolution
beginn-der-haitianischen-revolution#summ: In the French colony of Saint-Domingue, the enslaved rise up against their masters.
beginn-der-haitianischen-revolution#text: Through its sugar and coffee plantations, Saint-Domingue was the richest colony of France, in which half a million slaves worked under cruel conditions. The uprising of August 1791 grew under the leadership of Toussaint Louverture into a war lasting years, in which the insurgents held their own against the French, the Spanish, and the British. In 1794 France abolished slavery; after Napoleon's attempt to reintroduce it, Haiti declared its independence in 1804.
macartney-gesandtschaft#title: Macartney's embassy to the court of Qianlong
macartney-gesandtschaft#summary: A British embassy under Lord Macartney asks the Qianlong emperor in vain for better trading conditions and a permanent mission in Beijing.
macartney-gesandtschaft#text: Britain bought large quantities of tea in China but was only allowed to trade in Canton under strict rules. In 1793 Qianlong received the envoy George Macartney at his summer residence in Chengde, where Macartney bent only one knee instead of performing the full kowtow. Macartney presented gifts such as astronomical instruments and asked for additional ports and a permanent embassy. In an edict to King George III the emperor rejected all the requests, saying that China had no need of foreign goods. The failed contact became a prelude to later conflicts.
hinrichtung-ludwigs-xvi-und-schreckenshe: The execution of Louis XVI and the Reign of Terror
The king is guillotined, and the Committee of Public Safety under Robespierre establishes the rule of terror.

After his failed attempt to flee and the fall of the monarchy, Louis XVI was condemned for treason and executed on 21 January 1793. War against almost all of Europe, uprisings in the Vendée, and shortages of supplies led to the dictatorship of the Committee of Public Safety; by the summer of 1794 revolutionary tribunals had around 17,000 people executed, among them Queen Marie-Antoinette and Olympe de Gouges. In July 1794 Robespierre himself was overthrown and guillotined.
nizam-i-cedid#summary: Sultan Selim III raises an army trained on European lines and fails because of the resistance of the Janissaries.
nizam-i-cedid#text: After costly wars against Russia and Austria, Selim III had a new corps raised from 1793 that was trained by European officers and paid from a separate treasury. The "New Order" (Nizam-ı Cedid) also included engineering schools and the first permanent embassies in London, Paris, Vienna and Berlin. The Janissaries and parts of the clergy saw their position threatened. In 1807 a revolt toppled the sultan, who was murdered in 1808. His cousin Mahmud II later continued the reforms.
abschaffung-sklaverei-frankreich-1794#su: On 4 February 1794 the National Convention abolishes slavery in all French colonies, under the pressure of the uprising in Saint-Domingue.
abschaffung-sklaverei-frankreich-1794#te: Despite the Declaration of the Rights of Man, the National Assembly had at first left slavery in the colonies untouched, because planters and port cities profited from the sugar trade. Only the uprising in Saint-Domingue and the war against Spain and Great Britain forced the commissioners of the republic in 1793 to declare the enslaved free, in order to win them as soldiers. When a delegation from the colony, including the former slave Jean-Baptiste Belley, appeared before the Convention in February 1794, it resolved without a dissenting vote to abolish slavery in all colonies and to grant citizenship to all men regardless of the color of their skin. Napoleon reintroduced slavery in 1802, which rekindled the struggle for freedom in Haiti; France abolished it for good only in 1848.
napoleon-in-aegypten#summary: Napoleon occupies Egypt in order to strike at Great Britain's route to India; the campaign fails, but it founds the modern study of ancient Egypt.
napoleon-in-aegypten#text: In July 1798 Napoleon landed in Egypt with 35,000 soldiers; the country formally belonged to the Ottoman Empire but was ruled by the Mamluks, and he defeated their cavalry at the Battle of the Pyramids. A few days later the British fleet under Nelson destroyed the French ships at Aboukir, so that the army was cut off from supplies; an advance into Syria failed before Acre in 1799. Napoleon left his army secretly in order to seize power in Paris; the remnants surrendered to the British in 1801. The 167 scholars who had accompanied him surveyed temples, pyramids, and wildlife and published their results in the Description de l'Égypte; the Rosetta Stone, found in 1799, enabled Champollion to decipher the hieroglyphs in 1822. In Egypt itself the campaign set in motion the rise of Muhammad Ali and the modernization of the country.
code-civil#title: The Code civil comes into force
code-civil#summary: Napoleon gives France a uniform civil code that establishes equality before the law and freedom of property.
code-civil#text: The Code civil replaced hundreds of regional legal systems with a single code of more than 2,000 articles. It guaranteed the equality of all men before the law, freedom of contract and of trade, private property, and civil marriage, but it placed women under the guardianship of father or husband. It was introduced in the territories ruled by France, such as the Rhineland, the Netherlands, and Italy, and in part remained in force into the 20th century.
napoleon-kroent-sich-zum-kaiser#summary: In the cathedral of Notre-Dame, Napoleon Bonaparte places the imperial crown on his own head on 2 December 1804.
napoleon-kroent-sich-zum-kaiser#text: After the coup of 1799, Napoleon had stabilized France as First Consul and had himself confirmed by plebiscite. Pope Pius VII was present at the coronation, but Napoleon crowned himself and then his wife Joséphine, in order to show that he owed his power to no one. As Emperor of the French he led Europe into a decade of wars and reshaped the continent according to his will.
unabhaengigkeit-haitis#summary: On 1 January 1804 Jean-Jacques Dessalines declares the independence of Haiti, the first state founded by formerly enslaved people.
unabhaengigkeit-haitis#text: After Napoleon had sent an army to Saint-Domingue in 1802 to restore slavery, and after Toussaint Louverture had been carried off into captivity, Jean-Jacques Dessalines and Alexandre Pétion carried on the resistance. Yellow fever and the guerrilla warfare of the former slaves wore down the French troops; after the defeat at Vertières in November 1803 the French evacuated the colony. On 1 January 1804 Dessalines proclaimed independence at Gonaïves and gave the country its old indigenous name, Haiti; massacres of the remaining French followed. Haiti became the second independent state in the Americas, but it remained isolated by the slaveholding powers; France recognized it only in 1825, in return for an indemnity of 150 million francs that burdened the country for more than a century.
dschihad-usman-dan-fodio#title: Usman dan Fodio's jihad and the Sokoto Caliphate
dschihad-usman-dan-fodio#summary: The Fulani scholar Usman dan Fodio overthrows the Hausa kings and founds the Sokoto Caliphate, the largest state in West Africa in the 19th century.
dschihad-usman-dan-fodio#text: In the Hausa state of Gobir, Usman dan Fodio preached against the taxation, arbitrary rule and, in his view, imperfect Islam of the rulers. When the king moved against him, he left with his followers in 1804 and called for jihad, which many Fulani and Hausa peasants joined. By 1808 most of the Hausa cities had fallen, and in 1809 Sokoto became the capital of a caliphate with numerous emirates. Usman's son Muhammad Bello and his daughter Nana Asma'u built up administration and education. The caliphate lasted until the British conquest in 1903 and still shapes northern Nigeria today.
ende-des-heiligen-roemischen-reiches#tit: The end of the Holy Roman Empire
ende-des-heiligen-roemischen-reiches#sum: On 6 August 1806 Emperor Francis II lays down the imperial crown; the empire, more than 800 years old, ceases to exist.
ende-des-heiligen-roemischen-reiches#tex: After Austria's defeat at Austerlitz in 1805, Napoleon reordered Germany as he saw fit: Bavaria and Württemberg became kingdoms, and in July 1806 16 southern and western German states joined together under his protection in the Confederation of the Rhine and left the empire. As early as 1803, the Final Recess of the Imperial Deputation had dissolved the ecclesiastical principalities and most of the imperial cities and distributed their territories among larger states. In response to Napoleon's ultimatum, Francis II, who in 1804 had prudently raised himself to Emperor of Austria, declared the empire extinguished on 6 August 1806 and released all the estates from their obligations. The end of the empire, which had existed since Otto the Great, provoked hardly any resistance; Goethe noted that a quarrel involving his coachman had excited him more. The German question, how the many states should be joined together in future, remained open until 1871.
preussische-reformen#summary: After the defeat by Napoleon, Stein, Hardenberg, Scharnhorst, and Humboldt modernize the Prussian state from above.
preussische-reformen#text: In 1806 Napoleon had crushingly defeated the Prussian army at Jena and Auerstedt; the Peace of Tilsit in 1807 took half its territory from Prussia and forced it to make heavy payments. To save the state, the minister Baron vom Stein and, after him, Hardenberg began reforms intended to turn subjects into citizens: the October Edict of 1807 abolished the hereditary subjection of the peasants, the Municipal Ordinance of 1808 gave the towns self-government, in 1810 freedom of trade followed, and in 1812 the edict on the civil equality of the Jews. Scharnhorst and Gneisenau created an army of citizens that promoted officers by ability rather than by noble birth and received universal conscription in 1814; Wilhelm von Humboldt reformed the schools and founded the University of Berlin in 1810. The reforms remained unfinished, and a constitution was promised but not granted, yet they laid the foundation for Prussia's rise in the 19th century.
portugiesischer-hof-in-rio#title: The Portuguese court flees to Rio de Janeiro
portugiesischer-hof-in-rio#summary: Fleeing Napoleon's troops, the Portuguese royal family moves to Brazil, which thereby becomes the centre of the empire.
portugiesischer-hof-in-rio#text: When French troops advanced on Lisbon at the end of 1807, Prince Regent John left the country with the court, the government and the state treasury under British escort. In January 1808 he reached Bahia and opened the Brazilian ports to trade with friendly nations. In Rio de Janeiro a national library, a bank, a botanical garden and military schools were established. In 1815 Brazil was raised to a kingdom with equal status alongside Portugal. This elevation later eased the way to a more peaceful independence than in Spanish America.
mairevolution-buenos-aires#title: The May Revolution in Buenos Aires
mairevolution-buenos-aires#summary: On 25 May 1810 Creole citizens depose the viceroy and form a governing junta of their own.
mairevolution-buenos-aires#text: After Napoleon had deposed the Spanish king and occupied almost all of Spain, the citizens of Buenos Aires questioned the legitimacy of the viceroy. An open council meeting resolved to remove him, and on 25 May the First Junta met, which formally still governed in the name of the captive king. Similar juntas arose in 1810 in Caracas, Bogotá and Santiago de Chile. Paraguay, Upper Peru and Montevideo resisted the leadership of Buenos Aires, so that war and fragmentation followed. In 1816 the United Provinces in South America declared their independence at Tucumán.
russlandfeldzug-1812#summary: The Grande Armée marches on Moscow with more than 600,000 men and is almost completely destroyed on the retreat by cold, hunger, and fighting.
russlandfeldzug-1812#text: Because Tsar Alexander I no longer observed the Continental System against Great Britain, Napoleon crossed the Russian border on 24 June 1812 with the largest army Europe had ever seen; only a third of the soldiers were French, the rest Germans, Poles, Italians, and other allies. The Russians fell back and burned the land behind them, gave battle at Borodino on 7 September in the bloodiest engagement of the campaign, and abandoned Moscow, which went up in flames shortly after the French entered. Since the tsar would not negotiate, Napoleon ordered the retreat on 19 October, and with winter setting in early, with hunger and constant attacks by Cossacks, it became a catastrophe; at the crossing of the Berezina at the end of November the army finally fell apart. Barely more than 50,000 men returned. The defeat encouraged Prussia and Austria to ally with Russia and set off the Wars of Liberation.
voelkerschlacht-bei-leipzig#title: The Battle of the Nations at Leipzig
voelkerschlacht-bei-leipzig#summary: The armies of Russia, Prussia, Austria, and Sweden defeat Napoleon in the largest battle before the 20th century.
voelkerschlacht-bei-leipzig#text: After the destruction of the Grande Armée in Russia in 1812, Prussia and then Austria rose against French rule. From 16 to 19 October 1813 some 600,000 soldiers fought at Leipzig; more than 90,000 were killed or wounded. Napoleon had to withdraw across the Rhine, lost control of Germany, and abdicated in April 1814 after the allies marched into Paris.
wiener-kongress#summary: Under the direction of the Austrian foreign minister Metternich, the European powers reorder Europe after the fall of Napoleon.
wiener-kongress#text: Representatives of almost all the European states negotiated in Vienna over borders and forms of rule; the guiding ideas were the restoration of the old dynasties, a balance among the great powers, and solidarity against revolutions. In place of the Holy Roman Empire, dissolved in 1806, came the German Confederation of 39 states. The settlement protected Europe from major wars for decades, but it suppressed liberal and national movements with censorship and police.
schlacht-bei-waterloo#summary: Wellington and Blücher defeat Napoleon for good on 18 June 1815; he is banished to St Helena.
schlacht-bei-waterloo#text: In March 1815 Napoleon returned from the island of Elba to France, where the troops went over to him and Louis XVIII fled; the powers assembled in Vienna declared him an enemy of mankind. Napoleon attacked the armies standing in Belgium before they could unite, and on 16 June he defeated the Prussians at Ligny. On 18 June, at Waterloo south of Brussels, Wellington's British, Dutch, and German army withstood the French attacks all day, until in the evening Blücher's Prussians arrived and decided the issue; around 50,000 soldiers were killed or wounded. Napoleon abdicated for the second time and was taken by the British to the Atlantic island of St Helena, where he died in 1821. The rule of the Hundred Days was over, and the Second Peace of Paris imposed on France the loss of territory, occupation, and reparations.
shaka-gruendet-zulu-reich#summary: Shaka takes over the leadership of the Zulu and, with a newly organized army, makes them the strongest power in southeastern Africa.
